newsitem.title: UK: RESEARCH ALERT - Barclays cut at Lehman.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Barclays cut at Lehman.

text.p: Barclays Plc was cut to "neutral" from "outperform" at Lehman Brothers, the investment bank said on Thursday.

Analyst Robert Law at Lehman said the recent re-rating of Barclays shares "appears to have gone far enough" and that its current price-to-book multiple of 2.4 times seemed to be assuming a pick-up in growth "of which there is still little sign."
Law said he expected Barclays' first-half results to be subdued, due to a combination of weak volume growth and cost pressures at its investment banking arm BZW.
Without an acquisition or the rumoured disposal of BZW, he said he saw the shares -- which reached a record 13.12 stg in early trade on Thursday -- as high enough for the time being.

Separately, Law repeated a "buy" rating on HSBC Holdings Plc, arguing that the re-rating of the stock -- up 52 percent since early April to set a record 22.17 stg early on Thursday -- seemed likely to continue.
"In the long term, the bank looks well positioned to benefit from the growth in Far Eastern banking markets," Law said, "particularly in the personal sector."
He said HSBC was generating 20 percent return on equity and set a price target of 25.00 stg on the shares.
In a review of the British bank sector, Law also repeated "buy" ratings on Standard Chartered Plc and Lloyds TSB Group Plc.
He repeated "outperform" ratings on Abbey National Plc and Bank of Scotland Plc but rated National Westminster Bank Plc as "underperform."
The Lehman analyst said NatWest shares were "already more than discounting the relative profitability gains that we consider likely," adding that bid justification was unjustified.
